name: Idzing de la Kamtsha
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Mertens, Joseph. 1938. Les Ba Dzing de la Kamtsha. Deuxième partie: Grammaire de l'Idzing de la Kamtsha. (Institut Royal Colonial Belge, Section des Sciences morales et politiques, Mémoires in-8°, T. IV, fasc. 2.) Bruxelles: Librairie Falk fils / G. catalog_locator: Section I (La phonétique), Chapitre V (Quantité), § b. Accent, a) Accent dynamique, p. 23; b) Accent musical, p. 24.
catalog_quote: Il ne s'agit pas ici de l'accent de la phrase. Cet accent dépend de l'intention de celui qui parle, qui fait ressortir un bout de phrase dans son parler. Cela ne se réglemente pas. a) Accent dynamique. L'accent se marque très fortement en idzing. La syllabe du radical du mot porte l'accent. Ex.: i'kej, bi'suu, mu'kɔɔk, bumu'lal, baar ba'nna. Parfois on peut remarquer la présence d'un accent secondaire. La chose n'est pas précisément fréquente en idzing. Ex.: ije'bil = je t'ai appelé. Le préfixe ne portera donc jamais l'accent principal d'un mot, sauf quand l'assimilation l'a quasi fondu dans le radical. Ce sera le cas pour les monosyllabiques, tels que: bɔɔ, lɔɔ. Se rangent sous la même rubrique les radicaux monosyllabiques, dont le radical se réduit à une seule consonne. Ex.: buŋ. Cela n'empêche nullement le préfixe nasal d'être très fortement marqué comme dans: mpu, mbwa, ŋkwə, ŋyjɛp, ntsi, ntɔ. L'accent dynamique coïncidera souvent avec des syllabes longues. Il est en effet plus facile de soutenir un son fort qu'un son faible. Ex.: wu'naa, mi'njɔɔnsɔ, ba'kaar, ba m'bɛɛl. Dans les mots composés, comme dans les radicaux polysyllabiques, l'accent a une tendance à se rabattre sur la seconde syllabe. Ex.: maam'paŋ, naa n'tsɔŋ, taa'kɔɔm, ndzɔ ŋ'kaan.

new_statements.translation: Accent is very strongly marked in Idzing. The syllable of the word's radical (root) carries the accent. Ex.: i'kej, bi'suu, mu'kɔɔk, bumu'lal, baar ba'nna. Sometimes one can notice a secondary accent; this is not exactly frequent in Idzing. [...] The prefix will therefore never carry the main accent of a word, except when assimilation has practically fused it into the radical. [...] The dynamic accent will often coincide with long syllables. [...] In compound words, as in polysyllabic radicals, the accent tends to shift onto the second syllable. Ex.: maam'paŋ, naa n'tsɔŋ, taa'kɔɔm, ndzɔ ŋ'kaan.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word ('dynamic') stress falls on the root (radical) syllable, i.e. the first stem syllable after any class/agreement prefixes; prefixes are never stressed (unless fused into a monosyllable such as bɔɔ, lɔɔ); stress often coincides with long syllables; in compounds and polysyllabic roots stress tends to move to the second syllable (of the compound/root).
new_statements.secondary_stress: A secondary accent is occasionally noticeable but 'not exactly frequent' (ex. ije'bil 'I called you'); nasal prefixes can be strongly articulated without bearing accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllables where prefix has fused with root (bɔɔ, lɔɔ, buŋ) carry accent on that syllable; compounds and polysyllabic radicals tend to stress the second syllable. Author explicitly distinguishes this word accent from phrase accent, and separately notes an 'accent musical' (tone) that certainly exists in Idzing but which he could not study (p. 24).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level dynamic accent, explicitly set apart from phrase accent ('Il ne s'agit pas ici de l'accent de la phrase'). Tone ('accent musical') acknowledged as present and lexically relevant for monosyllables but left undescribed; a modern analysis would likely treat Ding as tonal (West-Coastal Bantu B86), so this 1938 stress statement is a missionary-era impressionistic description of stem-initial prominence.
new_statements.identity_note: Mertens 1938 describes 'idzing de la Kamtsha', the Ding variety spoken along the Kamtsha river (Kwilu, DR Congo) = Glottolog ding1239 (iso diz, Bantu B86). The Struyf 1939 sketch in T.IV-3 covers a different dialect (Kidinga of Mukene-Mbel) and has no accent statement. The earlier scan had named Mertens 1938 as 'not online'; it is in fact open at the Royal Academy for Overseas Sciences (kaowarsom.be) digitised memoirs, memoir_13.

sources.note: Section I (Phonétique), Ch. V §b 'Accent', pp. 23-24: dynamic accent is strongly marked; the root (radical) syllable carries the accent; prefixes never carry main accent (except when fused into monosyllables); secondary accent rare; accent often coincides with long syllables; in compounds and polysyllabic roots accent tends to fall on the second syllable. 'Accent musical' (tone) acknowledged to exist but not studied.
